text:
• Neutral language: When gathering feedback or presenting options, use
neutral language that doesn't lead respondents toward a particular choice.
For instance, rather than asking users if they "love" a new feature, ask how
they "feel" about it to get honest feedback.
• Gather more context: Acknowledge when you lack enough data to make an
informed decision and seek additional information to better understand the
situation.

Framing bias happens when people make choices based on how
information is shown, not the facts themselves.To avoid this, you can do
a few things:
First, look at information from different angles. For example, if 90% of
people like something, think about the 10% who don't. Second, ask
different people for their opinions to get a wider view. Third, use simple
and fair words when asking for feedback, like asking how someone feels
instead of if they love something. Lastly, if you don't have enough
information, look for more to help you decide better.
